verdict.rationale: The evidence pack has no Fastmail documentation or hands-on report about blocking tracking pixels or remote images by default, which is the core of this story. The only related item is one community remark that Fastmail is "up front with how the data is handled". That is an anecdotal comment on transparency, not a documented anti-tracking capability, so it is not enough for partial credit.

support.subject: As a switcher, the client protects me from senders' tracking — blocking read pixels by default — and is transparent about what it does with my mail data
